headline: Federal Government Launches $70 Million Passport Factory In Abuja
metaDescription: The Nigerian government has started building a $70 million passport production factory in Abuja, aiming for six million booklets every year by 2027.
aiSummaryBullets: The federal government has initiated construction of a $70 million passport manufacturing facility located in Abuja.
Projected completion is set for May 2027, with an initial output target of six million passport booklets annually.
Officials plan to eventually expand production capacity to ten million units and offer export services to other African nations.
aiContextParagraph: The Nigerian government has officially commenced the development of a major passport production centre in Abuja to address domestic document needs. The project, valued at $70 million, will be situated on a 1.1-hectare site. According to official reports, the facility is scheduled to reach completion by May 2027. Once fully operational, the plant is expected to produce six million passport booklets per year, with long-term plans in place to increase this capacity to 10 million units annually. Beyond meeting local demand, the government intends for the factory to serve as a regional hub, facilitating the export of passport booklets to other countries within Africa. This infrastructure investment marks a strategic shift toward domestic control of sensitive government document production, aiming to streamline availability and regional supply chain management.
whyItIsViral: This story is currently being covered by two independent national media outlets, reflecting a steady development in government infrastructure projects.
